card.name: The word "any" before plural nouns
card.fires_on: The word "any" used as a determiner after a verb or at the start of a request, right before a plural or uncountable noun such as references, news, questions, or symptoms.

modes.label: After a verb
modes.description: "any" follows a verb like cite, received, or experienced, in a negated or conditional clause.
modes.example: This article does not cite<< any>> references or sources.

modes.label: Opening a request
modes.description: "Any" begins a short invitation for input, such as feedback or news.
modes.example: Am I accurate?<< Any>> feedback would be helpful.”

card.writes: It favors plural, countable nouns such as subjects and characters, and disfavors singular nouns like consequence, complication, and thing.
card.plain: It marks the word "any" when a plural noun like questions, news, or symptoms is about to come next.
